root_cause.text: In stm32_usbphyc_probe, the bounds check for the device tree "reg" property used `>` instead of `>=`, allowing an index equal to the array size (`usbphyc->nphys`), which would cause an out-of-bounds access when indexing the `usbphyc->phys[]` array.
root_cause.evidence: The patch changes the comparison from `index > usbphyc->nphys` to `index >= usbphyc->nphys`. The commit message explicitly states: "if it is equal to usbphyc->nphys then it is one element out of bounds."

intent_record.intent_summary: Fix off-by-one error in STM32 USB PHY controller probe by changing the invalid index check from `>` to `>=` to prevent out-of-bounds access.
intent_record.what: Changed the condition from `index > usbphyc->nphys` to `index >= usbphyc->nphys` in the error check for the 'reg' property in the STM32 USB PHY controller probe function.
intent_record.how: This corrects an off-by-one error: previously, an index equal to the number of PHYs (nphys) was considered valid, which could lead to out-of-bounds array access. The fix ensures that only indices strictly less than nphys are accepted.

commit 94c358da3a0545205c6c6a50ae26141f1c73acfa
Author: Amelie Delaunay <amelie.delaunay@st.com>
Date:   Fri Mar 2 15:56:25 2018 +0100

    phy: stm32: add support for STM32 USB PHY Controller (USBPHYC)
    
    This patch adds phy transceiver driver for STM32 USB PHY Controller
    (USBPHYC) that provides dual port High-Speed phy for OTG (single port)
    and EHCI/OHCI host controller (two ports).
    One port of the phy is shared between the two USB controllers through
    a UTMI+ switch.
bic_trace_step.reason: The vulnerable check is clearly visible in the probe function at line 383: 'if (ret || index > usbphyc->nphys)'. Using '>' instead of '>=' allows index to equal usbphyc->nphys, causing an out-of-bounds access when indexing usbphyc->phys[port] later. The fix (using '>=') is not present.
